issues.evidence: P18: set-budget ' food ' stores 'food', then add 5 ' food ' -> 'unknown category' (B/budget_tracker.py:66 vs :97)
issues.summary: set-budget strips whitespace from category names but add does not, so the same input is accepted by one command and rejected by the other.

issues.evidence: static/B-ruff.txt: 28 findings (UP031 percent-format, B904, test F401/E741); B/budget_tracker.py:59 fixed .tmp name with no cleanup
issues.summary: Lint warnings, plus a fixed temp-file name that is not cleaned up if the write fails.

blinding_guess.why: B ships a test suite organised around each stated requirement (persist, unknown category, invalid amount, 80%, 100%, stdlib only), which suggests a requirement-driven process.

notes: Both use the same CLI shape (--file, set-budget, add, report --month) and Decimal money handling, so the probes ran unchanged on both. The two sides differ mainly in edge-case handling: A crashes on a structurally wrong data file, B validates structure but handles category whitespace inconsistently. Both crash on huge amounts. Bandit reported nothing for either side. The probes ran on Python 3.9.6.
